analysis.investment_thesis: Advanced Enzyme Technologies scores poorly on both Magic Formula pillars — earnings yield of ~5.8% (EBIT INR 196 Cr / EV ~INR 3,386 Cr) is below my 6% threshold, and ROIC of ~13.7% (EBIT/Invested Capital) falls well short of my 20% minimum for a "good business." You're paying a fair-to-full price for a business with structurally compressing returns.
key_strengths: Near-debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.02) with consistent positive OCF across all 5 years
High gross margin of 72% reflects genuine pricing power and proprietary enzyme IP
Diversified end-markets (healthcare, food, animal nutrition, industrial) reduce single-sector risk
key_risks: Severe margin compression: EBITDA fell from INR 260 Cr (FY21) to INR 223 Cr (FY25) even as revenue grew 27% — EBITDA CAGR only 4.7% vs revenue CAGR 9%
ROIC/ROCE at ~13% is mediocre for specialty chemicals; large equity base (INR 1,484 Cr) generating only INR 134 Cr net profit implies capital destruction at the margin
Earnings quality concern: Other Income surged to INR 33 Cr in FY25 (vs INR 3 Cr in FY16), masking weak operating performance
red_flags: Operating income CAGR (4.0%) dramatically lags revenue CAGR (9.0%) — nine-year divergence signals structural cost or competitive pressure
ROE of 9.54% is below India's 10-year risk-free rate (~7%) — this business is barely clearing its cost of equity
Other income (INR 33 Cr FY25) now represents ~25% of net profit — strip it out and earnings yield collapses further
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math tells the story quickly. EV ≈ INR 3,386 Cr (market cap INR 3,441 Cr + debt INR 39 Cr − cash INR 94 Cr). EBIT (operating income) is INR 196 Cr in FY25, giving an earnings yield of just 5.8% — below my 6% floor that defines "cheap." Invested capital (equity + debt − cash) is ~INR 1,429 Cr, so ROIC = 13.7%, confirmed by the reported ROCE of 13.1%. Neither metric clears the bar. On the Magic Formula ranking, this stock would be in the bottom half on both dimensions simultaneously — the worst possible outcome.

The business fundamentals compound the concern. Revenue has grown at a respectable 9% CAGR over nine years, but EBITDA grew at only 4.7% and net profit at 6.3%, meaning every incremental rupee of revenue is generating less profit than before. Operating income actually peaked at INR 232 Cr in FY21 and has *contracted* to INR 196 Cr in FY25 despite revenue expanding from INR 502 Cr to INR 637 Cr. Meanwhile the equity base has ballooned from INR 839 Cr to INR 1,484 Cr — retained earnings are being ploughed back at below-market returns, which is value-destructive. At P/E 23.9x with these deteriorating economics, the stock is priced for a quality business it no longer resembles.
